abstract: The epidemiology of testicular cancer (TC) has 2 distinguishing features. First, it has an unusual unimodal age-incidence curve which peaks about age 30, and decreases with increasing age. Second, risk of the disease has been consistently associated with a high standard of living inasmuch as it is a disease of young white men of generally higher social class in economically developed populations. These features suggest that risk may be related to relatively late age of exposure to common infectious agents resulting in damage to the developing testis. We evaluated this hypothesis in a serologic case-control study in which subjects were compared for both prevalence and level of antibody to the following agents: measles, mumps, rubella, varicella (VZV), herpes simplex (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), toxoplasmosis, Chlamydia, and Mycoplasma hominis. The TC cases included 50 with seminoma, 50 with embryonal carcinoma, and 17 with other sub-classifications. There were 100 male controls of comparable age. No consistent differences were found for any of the non-herpes viruses. For VZV, cases generally had elevated titers, significantly so for the seminoma patients, relative risk (RR) = 6.3 (95% confidence interval, 3.0-13.3) adjusted for the titer distributions of HSV and CMV. For HSV, seminoma patients also had elevated titers, RR = 2.6 (1.0-6.4). The strongest association was with CMV. Patients had a higher prevalence rate than controls, RR = 2.0 (1.1-3.6), and a gradient of risk with titer level. Overall, those in the highest titer quartile had an RR of 4.9 compared to those with no antibody, with a significant trend (p = 0.0002). Since age at CMV infection is directly related to social class, these findings suggest that delayed exposure to CMV, resulting in a more severe infection, may be related to risk of TC. However, confounding by immune status of the cases or by other risk factors of TC could not be evaluated and may account for this observation.
abstract_ja: 精巣がん患者は、年齢を合わせた男性対照と比較して、いくつかのウイルス感染に対する抗体の有病率と抗体価が異なるかを検討した。血清学的症例対照研究として、麻疹、流行性耳下腺炎、風疹、水痘帯状疱疹ウイルス（VZV）、単純ヘルペスウイルス（HSV）、サイトメガロウイルス（CMV）、トキソプラズマ、クラミジア、マイコプラズマ・ホミニスに対する抗体の有病率と抗体価を比較した。精巣がん症例はセミノーマ50例、胎児性癌50例、その他の亜分類17例であった。対照は年齢の合った男性100例であった。ヘルペス以外のウイルスでは一貫した差は認められなかった。VZVについては、症例は全体に抗体価が高く、特にセミノーマ患者で有意であった（HSVおよびCMVの抗体価分布で調整した相対危険度（RR）= 6.3, 95%信頼区間 3.0-13.3）。HSVについてもセミノーマ患者で抗体価が高かった（RR = 2.6, 1.0-6.4）。最も強い関連はCMVで認められた。症例の有病率は対照より高く（RR = 2.0, 1.1-3.6）、抗体価の高さに応じたリスクの勾配が見られた。全体として、抗体価が最も高い四分位群は抗体が無い群と比べてRR 4.9であり、有意な傾向が認められた（p = 0.0002）。CMVへの感染時期は社会階級と直接関連するため、これらの所見は、CMVへの曝露が遅れ、より重篤な感染を起こしたことが精巣がんのリスクに関連している可能性を示唆する。ただし、症例の免疫状態や他のリスク因子による交絡は評価できず、この観察結果を説明しうる。
